async def watch(self, stop: asyncio.Event) -> None:
        review = self.ctx.review.path.name

        async def follow(paths, recursive: bool, keep):
            async for batch in watchfiles.awatch(*paths, recursive=recursive, debounce=120, step=40, stop_event=stop, watch_filter=keep):
                change = await asyncio.to_thread(self.changed, {p for _, p in batch})
                if change:
                    for q in list(self.subscribers):
                        q.put_nowait(change)

        await asyncio.gather(
            follow(self.watched(), True, lambda _, p: p.endswith((".rs", ".py", ".md"))),
            # The review file is at the root, which is too big to watch whole
            follow([self.ctx.root], False, lambda _, p: Path(p).name == review),
        )

def watched(self) -> list[Path]:
        """The folders the globs look in: each glob up to its first wildcard.

        Returns
        -------
        list of Path
            The folders, any inside another left out.
        """
        dirs = set()
        for g in [*self.ctx.config.sources, *self.ctx.spec.globs, *self.ctx.config.docs]:
            fixed = []
            for part in Path(g).parts:
                if any(c in part for c in "*?["):
                    break
                fixed.append(part)
            path = self.ctx.root.joinpath(*fixed)
            dirs.add(path if path.is_dir() else path.parent)
        # Drop any folder inside another
        return sorted(d for d in dirs if not any(o != d and o in d.parents for o in dirs))

# r[impl ref.nearest]
    def nearest(self, ref: str, n: int = 5) -> list[Symbol]:
        """The symbols `ref` most likely meant.

        Names close to its last part, best first by how closely the whole of it matches the
        end of theirs.

        Parameters
        ----------
        ref : str
            The reference that didn't resolve.
        n : int
            How many to return, at most.

        Returns
        -------
        list of Symbol
            Best first.
        """
        from difflib import SequenceMatcher, get_close_matches

        want = ref.split("::")
        tail = want[-1]
        pool = [s for s in self.symbols if s.kind != "impl"]
        close = set(get_close_matches(tail, list({s.name for s in pool}), n=25, cutoff=0.6))

        def score(s: Symbol) -> float:
            name = SequenceMatcher(None, tail.lower(), s.name.lower()).ratio()
            whole = SequenceMatcher(None, ref.lower(), "::".join(s.segments[-len(want) :]).lower()).ratio()
            return name + whole

        return sorted((s for s in pool if s.name in close), key=score, reverse=True)[:n]

def refresh(self) -> bool:
        """Re-read changed files.

        Returns
        -------
        bool
            Whether anything changed, a file added or gone included.
        """
        changed = False
        current = {}
        for p in self.paths():
            rel = str(p.relative_to(self.root))
            mtime = p.stat().st_mtime
            cached = self._by_file.get(rel)
            if cached and cached[0] == mtime:
                current[rel] = cached
                continue
            parser, index = self.parsers[p.suffix]
            current[rel] = (mtime, index(rel, p.read_bytes(), parser))
            changed = True
        if set(current) != set(self._by_file):
            changed = True
        self._by_file = current
        if changed:
            self.symbols = [s for _, syms in current.values() for s in syms]
            self._traces = None
        return changed

    # r[impl ref.ambiguous]
    # r[impl ref.crate]
    def resolve(self, ref: str) -> tuple[Symbol | None, list[Symbol]]:
        """The one symbol `ref` names, or None and the candidates.

        The candidates are several if it's ambiguous, the nearest few if there's none.

        `ref` is a tail of a qualified name (`BatteryController::on_site_load`), or a file
        and a name inside it (`src/v2/fleet.rs#BatteryUpdate::Short`).

        Parameters
        ----------
        ref : str
            The reference, as written.

        Returns
        -------
        symbol : Symbol or None
            The symbol, if exactly one matches.
        candidates : list of Symbol
            Empty if it resolved; else the matches, or the nearest names.
        """
        file = None
        if "#" in ref:
            file, ref = ref.split("#", 1)
        # A file is its path from the root, or any tail of it: `lib.rs`, `controller/mod.rs`
        pool = (
            [s for rel, (_, syms) in self._by_file.items() if rel == file or rel.endswith("/" + file) for s in syms]
            if file
            else self.symbols
        )
        if ref.startswith("impl "):
            return self._resolve_impl(ref, pool)
        # `crate::` anchors it at the root: the whole qualified name, not a tail of it
        anchored = ref.startswith("crate::")
        want = ref.removeprefix("crate::").split("::")
        hits = [s for s in pool if s.kind != "impl" and (s.segments == want if anchored else s.segments[-len(want) :] == want)]
        # A method and a field can share a name: the method is what's meant, unless the
        # reference says `field:`
        items = [s for s in hits if s.kind not in ("field",)]
        if len(hits) > 1 and len(items) == 1:
            return items[0], []
        if len(hits) == 1:
            return hits[0], []
        if len(hits) > 1:
            return None, hits
        return None, self.nearest(ref)

def shortest_unique(self, sym: Symbol) -> str:
        """The shortest tail of its qualified name that names only it.

        A method, field or variant keeps its owner (`Dispatch::on_short`, not `on_short`) so
        it reads well where it's written; an impl block is `impl` and its type.

        Parameters
        ----------
        sym : Symbol
            The symbol.

        Returns
        -------
        str
            The reference to write; its qualified name if no shorter tail is unique.
        """
        segs = sym.segments
        if sym.kind == "impl":
            label = segs[-1][1:-1]  # "impl Trait for Type" or "impl Type"
            trait = label[len("impl ") :].rpartition(" for ")[0]
            path = segs[:-1]
            for k in range(1, len(path) + 1):
                tail = path[-k:] + [segs[-1]]
                if sum(1 for s in self.symbols if s.kind == "impl" and s.segments[-len(tail) :] == tail) == 1:
                    return f"impl {trait + ' for ' if trait else ''}{'::'.join(path[-k:])}"
            return f"impl {trait + ' for ' if trait else ''}{'::'.join(path)}"
        member = len(segs) > 1 and segs[-2][:1].isupper()
        for k in range(2 if member else 1, len(segs) + 1):
            tail = segs[-k:]
            if sum(1 for s in self.symbols if s.kind != "impl" and s.segments[-k:] == tail) == 1:
                return "::".join(tail)
        return sym.qualified

    def traces(self) -> dict[str, list[Trace]]:
        """For each requirement ID, the markers that name it, in file and line order.

        Returns
        -------
        dict of str to list of Trace
            By requirement ID; each with the smallest symbol around it, if any.
        """
        if self._traces is None:
            out: dict[str, list[Trace]] = {}
            for rel, (_, syms) in sorted(self._by_file.items()):
                spans = [s for s in syms if s.kind not in ("impl", "field")]
                for n, line in enumerate(self.files.lines(rel), start=1):
                    if "[" not in line:
                        continue
                    for m in MARKER.finditer(line):
                        around = [s for s in spans if s.start <= n <= s.end]
                        sym = min(around, key=lambda s: s.end - s.start, default=None)
                        rid = tracey.key(m.group(1), m.group(3))
                        version = int(m.group(4) or 1)
                        trace = Trace(kind=m.group(2), requirement=rid, version=version, file=rel, line=n, symbol=sym)
                        out.setdefault(rid, []).append(trace)
            self._traces = out
        return self._traces

    def mentions(self) -> re.Pattern | None:
        """A pattern for every term as it's written in prose, but those cited only.

        Longest first, singular or plural, whole words only, ignoring case.

        Returns
        -------
        re.Pattern or None
            None if no terms are to be found in prose.
        """
        if self._pattern is None:
            words = sorted((d.words for d in self.terms.values() if not d.cited_only), key=len, reverse=True)
            alts = "|".join(re.escape(w).replace(r"\ ", r"[ \-]") for w in words)
            self._pattern = re.compile(rf"\b({alts})(?:s|es)?\b", re.IGNORECASE) if words else None
        return self._pattern

    def of(cls, ctx: Context) -> Library:

        out: dict[str, Summary] = {}
        for rel in rels:
            w = Walk(ctx, rel)
            problems = w.problems()
            reviewed, embedded = w.reviewed_count()
            out[rel] = Summary(
                rel=rel,
                weight=w.meta.weight,
                title=w.title,
                summary=w.summary,
                tags=sorted(set(w.meta.tags)),
                folder=str(PurePosixPath(rel).parent),
                links_to=[l for l in w.links if l in known],
                references=len(w.refs),
                embedded=embedded,
                reviewed=reviewed,
                broken=sum(1 for p in problems if p.severity == "error"),
                changed=sum(1 for p in problems if p.severity == "warning"),
                kind=w.meta.kind,
                stage=(w.meta.stage or "problem") if w.meta.kind == "prd" else None,
                **w.progress().model_dump(),
            )
        for s in out.values():
            for target in s.links_to:
                out[target].linked_from.append(s.rel)
        specs = []
        for rel in ctx.spec_paths():
            v = prose.view(ctx, rel)
            uncited = len(v.uncited)
            specs.append(
                SpecSummary(
                    rel=rel,
                    weight=(sw := Walk(ctx, rel)).meta.weight,
                    title=sw.title,
                    requirements=len(v.defined),
                    cited=len(v.defined) - uncited,
                    uncited=uncited,
                    missing=len(v.missing),
                    drifted=len(v.drifted),
                )
            )
        return cls(codewalks=list(out.values()), specs=specs)

# r[impl embed.current]
    # r[impl ref.sig]
    # r[impl review.changed]
    def embed(self, ref: Ref) -> str:
        if ref.requirement:
            return self.requirement(ref, ref.requirement)
        if not ref.symbol:
            index = self.ctx.index
            ambiguous = ref.candidates and all(c.name == ref.target.split("::")[-1] for c in ref.candidates)
            return templates.get_template("broken.html").render(
                ref=ref,
                ambiguous=ambiguous,
                candidates=[(index.shortest_unique(c), f"{c.file}:{c.line}") for c in ref.candidates],
            )
        s = ref.symbol
        files = self.ctx.index.files
        self.symbols[ref.key] = symbol_data(self.walk, s)
        self.note_requirements(m[1] for m in s.markers)
        highlighted = highlight_lines(self.ctx.root / s.file)
        # `sig`: the runs of lines its outline gives, or its doc comments and first line
        runs = (s.outline or [(s.start, s.line)]) if ref.sig else [(s.start, s.end)]
        shown = [n for a, b in runs for n in range(a, b + 1)]
        raw = [files.lines(s.file)[n - 1] for n in shown]
        last = shown[-1]
        for line in raw:
            self.note_requirements([tracey.key(p, rid) for p, _, rid, _ in REQ_IN_CODE.findall(line)])
        # Shown without the indent it has inside its impl, class or module
        indent = min((len(l) - len(l.lstrip()) for l in raw if l.strip()), default=0)
        # A gap between runs is a row of its own, with no line number
        rows = []
        for n in shown:
            if rows and rows[-1][0] is not None and n != rows[-1][0] + 1:
                rows.append((None, Markup("…")))
            rows.append((n, Markup(_dedent_html(highlighted[n - 1], indent) or " ")))
        more = last < s.end
        digest = s.digest(files)
        reviewed = self.ctx.review.get(self.walk.rel, ref.key)
        state = "new" if reviewed is None else ("changed" if reviewed.digest != digest else "ok")
        return templates.get_template("figure.html").render(
            ref=ref,
            s=s,
            rows=rows,
            digest=digest,
            state=state,
            diff=diff_rows(reviewed.text, s.text(files)) if state == "changed" else None,
            plan=diff_rows(ref.draft or "", "\n".join(l[indent:] for l in raw), context=3) if ref.settled else None,
            more=more,
            parts=path_parts(s.qualified),
            zed=self.symbols[ref.key]["zed"],
            slug=_slug(ref.key),
        )

# r[impl proposal.change]
    def proposal(self, ref: Ref, end: int) -> str:
        """A `walk proposed` block: the draft, or once the name exists, what was written.

        Once it's written, the draft is shown against it.

        Parameters
        ----------
        ref : Ref
            The proposal.
        end : int
            The block's last line in the Markdown.

        Returns
        -------
        str
            The HTML.
        """
        files = self.ctx.index.files
        draft_rows = [Markup(h or " ") for h in highlight_text(ref.draft or "", ref.lang)]
        rows, diff = None, None
        if s := ref.symbol:
            self.symbols[ref.target] = symbol_data(self.walk, s)
            highlighted = highlight_lines(self.ctx.root / s.file)
            raw = files.lines(s.file)[s.start - 1 : s.end]
            indent = min((len(l) - len(l.lstrip()) for l in raw if l.strip()), default=0)
            rows = [(n, Markup(_dedent_html(highlighted[n - 1], indent) or " ")) for n in range(s.start, s.end + 1)]
            current = "\n".join(l[indent:] for l in raw)
            # A change shows what there is, then what there will be; a written proposal what
            # was planned, then what was written
            diff = diff_rows(current, ref.draft or "", context=3) if ref.change else diff_rows(ref.draft or "", current, context=3)
        # Taken: the name is already several symbols' (not just close to some)
        ambiguous = len(ref.candidates) > 1 and all(c.name == ref.target.split("::")[-1] for c in ref.candidates)
        return templates.get_template("proposal.html").render(
            ref=ref,
            s=ref.symbol,
            parts=path_parts(ref.symbol.qualified if ref.symbol else ref.target),
            draft=draft_rows,
            rows=rows,
            diff=diff,
            end=end,
            ambiguous=ambiguous,
            agreed=None if ref.symbol else self.walk.agreement(ref),
            candidates=[self.ctx.index.shortest_unique(c) for c in ref.candidates] if ambiguous else [],
            zed=self.symbols[ref.target]["zed"] if ref.symbol else None,
            slug=_slug(ref.target),
        )

def render(self) -> tuple[str, dict]:
        md = self.walk.md
        rules = md.renderer.rules
        rules["fence"] = self.fence
        rules["walk_ref"] = lambda tokens, idx, options, env: self.inline_ref(
            tokens[idx].meta["target"], tokens[idx].meta["label"], env["line"]
        )
        rules["link_open"] = self.link_open
        rules["link_close"] = self.link_close
        rules["front_matter"] = lambda *a: ""
        rules["code_inline"] = self.code_inline
        rules["text"] = self.text

        tokens = self.walk.tokens
        found = {start: (close, t) for start, close, t in threads(tokens)}
        out = []
        env: dict = {"line": 0}
        i = 0
        while i < len(tokens):
            if i in found:
                close, thread = found[i]
                out.append(self.thread(i, close, thread, env))
                i = close + 1
                continue
            j = i
            while j < len(tokens) and j not in found:
                j += 1
            out.extend(self.render_tokens(tokens[i:j], env))
            i = j
        return "".join(out), {"symbols": self.symbols, "requirements": self.requirements, "terms": self.definitions}

    rel: str

    weight: int | None = None
    title: str
    summary: str | None
    tags: list[str]
    # Its folder, which is how the index groups codewalks
    folder: str

    links_to: list[str]
    linked_from: list[str] = []
    references: int
    embedded: int
    reviewed: int
    broken: int
    changed: int
    # "prd", say, from its front matter
    kind: str | None = None
    # For a PRD, its stage, from its front matter
    stage: Stage | None = None
    # Its proposals: not written yet, written, settled
    proposed: int = 0
    written: int = 0
    settled: int = 0

    # r[impl proposal.progress+2]
    @property
    def plan(self) -> int:
        return self.proposed + self.written + self.settled

    @property
    def plan_status(self) -> str:
        if not self.plan:
            return ""
        return "proposed" if self.proposed == self.plan else "done" if self.settled == self.plan else "in progress"

    @property
    def reviewed_pct(self) -> int:
        return int(100 * self.reviewed / self.embedded) if self.embedded else 100

class Symbol(BaseModel):
    """One thing a codewalk can point at."""

    qualified: str
    kind: str
    file: str
    # 1-based, inclusive. `start` takes in its doc comments, attributes and markers
    start: int
    line: int
    end: int
    signature: str
    doc: str
    # Requirement markers on it, `impl` or `verify`, with their IDs and the versions they
    # name, 1 without a suffix
    markers: list[tuple[str, str, int]] = []
    # The rest of its documentation after the summary: for Python, a NumPy-style
    # docstring's extended summary and sections (Parameters, Returns, …)
    details: str = ""
    # What `sig` shows, as runs of lines (1-based, inclusive), if more than its doc
    # comments and first line: for Python, a def's header and docstring; a class's, with
    # its fields and its `__init__`'s header and docstring
    outline: list[tuple[int, int]] = []

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        return self.qualified.rsplit("::", 1)[-1]

    @property
    def segments(self) -> list[str]:
        return self.qualified.split("::")

    def text(self, files: SourceFiles) -> str:
        return "\n".join(files.lines(self.file)[self.start - 1 : self.end])

    def digest(self, files: SourceFiles) -> str:
        return hashlib.sha256(self.text(files).encode()).hexdigest()[:12]

    def _proposal(self, tok) -> Ref:
        """A `walk proposed` block, or `walk proposed change`: the name, then the draft."""
        lines = tok.content.rstrip("\n").split("\n")
        first = next((i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l.strip()), 0)
        words = tok.info.split()
        change = len(words) > 2 and words[2] == "change"
        lang = words[3 if change else 2] if len(words) > (3 if change else 2) else None
        line = (tok.map[0] + 2 + first) if tok.map else 0
        ref = Ref(
            target=lines[first].strip() if lines else "",
            kind="proposal",
            line=line,
            proposed=True,
            change=change,
            draft="\n".join(lines[first + 1 :]).strip("\n"),
            lang=lang,
        )
        return self._resolve(ref)

# r[impl proposal.settle]
    def _settled(self, tok) -> Ref | None:
        """A `walk settled` block: a proposal that's been written.

        The code as written is shown, as in a `walk` block, and the draft is kept, to show
        how it differed.

        Parameters
        ----------
        tok : Token
            The fence.

        Returns
        -------
        Ref or None
            The reference, resolved; None if the block names nothing.
        """
        lines = tok.content.rstrip("\n").split("\n")
        first = next((i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l.strip()), None)
        if first is None or not (parsed := embed_line(lines[first])):
            return None
        target, focus, sig = parsed
        words = tok.info.split()
        ref = Ref(
            target=target,
            kind="embed",
            line=(tok.map[0] + 2 + first) if tok.map else 0,
            focus=focus,
            sig=sig,
            settled=True,
            draft="\n".join(lines[first + 1 :]).strip("\n"),
            lang=words[2] if len(words) > 2 else None,
        )
        return self._resolve(ref)

# r[impl export.plain]
    def export(self, out_rel: str) -> str:
        """The codewalk as plain Markdown, for anywhere that won't run this.

        Each embedded symbol becomes a link to it and its code, and each inline one a link.

        Parameters
        ----------
        out_rel : str
            Where it'll be written, from the root, so its links are relative to there.

        Returns
        -------
        str
            The Markdown.
        """
        files = self.ctx.index.files
        base = (self.ctx.root / out_rel).parent

        def link(file: str, line: int) -> str:
            return os.path.relpath(self.ctx.root / file, base) + f"#L{line}"

        embeds = {r.line: r for r in self.embeds}
        proposals = {r.line - 1: r for r in self.refs if r.kind == "proposal"}
        out_lines = []
        lines = self.text.split("\n")
        i = 0
        while i < len(lines):
            line = lines[i]
            if line.strip().startswith("```walk settled"):
                j = i + 1
                while j < len(lines) and lines[j].strip() != "```":
                    j += 1
                ref = next((embeds[n] for n in range(i + 2, j + 1) if n in embeds), None)
                if ref and (sym := ref.symbol):
                    code = "\n".join(files.lines(sym.file)[sym.start - 1 : sym.end])
                    ind = min((len(l) - len(l.lstrip())) for l in code.split("\n") if l.strip())
                    code = "\n".join(l[ind:] for l in code.split("\n"))
                    out_lines.append(f"[`{sym.file}:{sym.line}`]({link(sym.file, sym.line)})\n\n```{fence_lang(sym.file)}\n{code}\n```")
                i = j + 1
                continue
            if line.strip().startswith("```walk proposed"):
                j = i + 1
                while j < len(lines) and lines[j].strip() != "```":
                    j += 1
                ref = next((r for r in proposals.values() if i < r.line - 1 <= j), None)
                if ref and ref.symbol:
                    out_lines.append(
                        f"[`{ref.symbol.file}:{ref.symbol.line}`]({link(ref.symbol.file, ref.symbol.line)}) (proposed, now written)"
                    )
                elif ref:
                    out_lines.append(f"**Proposed:** `{ref.target}`, not written yet\n\n```{ref.lang or ''}\n{ref.draft}\n```")
                i = j + 1
                continue
            if line.strip() == "```walk":
                j = i + 1
                blocks = []
                while j < len(lines) and lines[j].strip() != "```":
                    if ref := embeds.get(j + 1):
                        if req := ref.requirement:
                            blocks.append(f"> [`{req.id}`]({link(req.file, req.line)}): {req.text}")
                        elif sym := ref.symbol:
                            last = sym.line if ref.sig else sym.end
                            code = "\n".join(files.lines(sym.file)[sym.start - 1 : last])
                            ind = min((len(l) - len(l.lstrip())) for l in code.split("\n") if l.strip())
                            code = "\n".join(l[ind:] for l in code.split("\n"))
                            blocks.append(
                                f"[`{sym.file}:{sym.line}`]({link(sym.file, sym.line)})\n\n```{fence_lang(sym.file)}\n{code}\n```"
                            )
                        else:
                            blocks.append(f"> **Unresolved:** `{ref.key}`")
                    j += 1
                out_lines.append("\n\n".join(blocks))
                i = j + 1
                continue

            def wiki(m):
                target, label = m.group(1).strip(), (m.group(2) or "").strip()
                if target.startswith("r:"):
                    r = self.ctx.spec.find(target[2:], self.rel)
                    return f"[`{label or target[2:]}`]({link(r.file, r.line)})" if r else f"`{target[2:]}`"
                sym, _ = self.ctx.index.resolve(target)
                return f"[`{label or (sym.name if sym else target)}`]({link(sym.file, sym.line)})" if sym else f"`{label or target}`"

            def walk_link(m):
                sym, _ = self.ctx.index.resolve(m.group(2))
                return f"[{m.group(1)}]({link(sym.file, sym.line)})" if sym else m.group(1)

            line = WIKI.sub(wiki, line)
            line = re.sub(r"\[([^\]]+)\]\(walk:([^)\s]+)\)", walk_link, line)
            out_lines.append(line)
            i += 1
        header = f"<!-- Exported from {self.rel} by codewalk: edit that, not this -->\n\n"
        return header + "\n".join(out_lines)

def _leading(node: Node, siblings: list[Node]) -> list[Node]:
    """The comments and attributes directly above `node`, with no blank line between.

    `siblings` are its parent's children. They're in order, first to last: its span starts
    at the first. Found by position, not `prev_sibling`, which crashes this version of
    tree-sitter.

    Parameters
    ----------
    node : Node
        The item.
    siblings : list of Node
        Its parent's children, unnamed ones included.

    Returns
    -------
    list of Node
        The comments and attributes, first to last; a `//!` comment stops them.
    """
    i = next(k for k, s in enumerate(siblings) if s.start_byte == node.start_byte and s.type == node.type)
    above: list[Node] = []
    top_row = node.start_point.row
    for prev in reversed(siblings[:i]):
        if prev.type not in ("line_comment", "block_comment", "attribute_item"):
            break
        # A line comment's span takes in its newline, so it ends at column 0 of the next row
        end_row = prev.end_point.row - (1 if prev.end_point.column == 0 else 0)
        if end_row < top_row - 1:
            break
        if prev.type == "line_comment" and (prev.text or b"").startswith(b"//!"):
            break
        above.append(prev)
        top_row = prev.start_point.row
    above.reverse()
    return above

# r[impl spec.cite]
def cited_ids(text: str, known: SpecIndex, rel: str | None = None) -> list[str]:
    """The requirement IDs a block of prose cites, in order.

    That's backticked IDs that are requirements (or look like them, and are cited as such
    elsewhere), `[[r:…]]`, and `(req:…)` links.

    Parameters
    ----------
    text : str
        The block's Markdown.
    known : SpecIndex
        Every requirement; a backticked ID counts only if it's one.
    rel : str or None
        The file the prose is in, for IDs written without their spec's name.

    Returns
    -------
    list of str
        The IDs, each once.
    """
    out: list[str] = []
    for m in CITE_CODE.finditer(text):
        if r := known.find(m.group(1), rel):
            out.append(r.id)
    # `[[r:id]]` or a link, in backticks, is an example of one, not a citation
    bare = re.sub(r"(`+)(?:(?!\1).)+\1", "", text)
    written = [m.group(1).strip()[2:] for m in WIKI.finditer(bare) if m.group(1).strip().startswith("r:")]
    for rid in written + CITE_LINK.findall(bare):
        r = known.find(rid, rel)
        out.append(r.id if r else rid)
    return list(dict.fromkeys(out))

# r[impl note.resolve]
def compact(thread: Thread, date: str, about: list[str] | None = None) -> str:
    """A settled thread as one changelog line: what was asked, and how it was settled.

    Parameters
    ----------
    thread : Thread
        The thread.
    date : str
        When it was resolved, as ``YYYY-MM-DD``.
    about : list of str, optional
        The names it was about, if it sat under an excerpt.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        A Markdown list item. Any notes between the first and the one that settled it are
        counted, not kept.
    """
    notes = thread.all()
    first = notes[0]
    last = next((n for n in reversed(notes) if n.kind in ("done", "decision", "answer")), notes[-1])

    def said(n: Note) -> str:
        who = f" @{n.author}" if n.author else ""
        return f"**{n.kind}**{who}: {_sentence(n.text)}"

    line = f"- {date}"
    if about:
        line += " (" + ", ".join(f"`{a}`" for a in about) + ")"
    line += f": {said(first)}"
    if last is not first:
        line += f" → {said(last)}"
    between = len(notes) - (2 if last is not first else 1)
    if between > 0:
        line += f" ({between} more note{'s' if between > 1 else ''})"
    return line

def diff_rows(before: str, after: str, context: int = 2) -> list[dict]:
    """What changed, as the changed lines with a little context either side.

    Runs of unchanged lines between them collapse to a gap saying how many.

    Parameters
    ----------
    before, after : str
        The text before and after.
    context : int
        How many unchanged lines to keep either side of a change.

    Returns
    -------
    list of dict
        Rows for the diff template: `del`, `add` or `same` with the line, or `gap` with a count.
    """
    lines = diff(before, after)
    near = {j for i, (tag, _) in enumerate(lines) if tag != " " for j in range(i - context, i + context + 1)}
    rows, skipped = [], 0
    for i, (tag, text) in enumerate(lines):
        if i not in near:
            skipped += 1
            continue
        if skipped:
            rows.append({"kind": "gap", "count": skipped})
            skipped = 0
        rows.append({"kind": {"-": "del", "+": "add", " ": "same"}[tag], "tag": tag, "text": text})
    if skipped:
        rows.append({"kind": "gap", "count": skipped})
    return rows

    It becomes a `walk settled` block, which shows `target`'s code as written and keeps the
    draft, so what was planned and what happened can both be seen.

    return target.strip(), focus.strip() or None, sig

def describe(ctx: Context, target: str) -> tuple[str, tuple[str, int]] | None:
    """Markdown describing what `target` names, and where it is.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ctx : Context
        The project.
    target : str
        A reference: a symbol, or `r:`, `t:` or `f:` and an ID.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple of (str, tuple of (str, int)) or None
        The Markdown, and the file and line it's defined at; None if nothing by that name.
    """
    if target.startswith(("t:", "f:")):
        d = ctx.glossary.get(target)
        if not d:
            return None
        status = f" · *{d.status}*" if d.status else ""
        return f"**{d.kind}** `{d.id}`{status}\n\n{d.text}\n\n{d.file}:{d.line}", (d.file, d.line)
    if target.startswith("r:"):
        r = ctx.spec.find(target[2:])
        if not r:
            return None
        traces = ctx.index.traces().get(r.id, [])
        code = "\n".join(f"- {t.kind}: `{ctx.index.shortest_unique(t.symbol) if t.symbol else t.file}` ({t.file}:{t.line})" for t in traces)
        return f"**requirement** `{r.id}`\n\n{r.text}\n\n{code}\n\n{r.file}:{r.line}", (r.file, r.line)
    sym, _ = ctx.index.resolve(target.split(" > ")[0])
    if not sym:
        return None
    markers = ", ".join(f"{k} {i}" + (f"+{v}" if v > 1 else "") for k, i, v in sym.markers)
    return (
        f"**{sym.kind}** `{sym.qualified}`\n\n```\n{sym.signature}\n```\n\n{sym.doc}\n\n"
        + (f"```text\n{sym.details}\n```\n\n" if sym.details else "")
        + f"{markers}\n\n{sym.file}:{sym.line}",
        (sym.file, sym.line),
    )

# r[impl ref.focus]
def narrow(sym: Symbol, focus: str, files: SourceFiles) -> Symbol | None:
    """The part of `sym` that starts at the first line containing `focus`.

    It takes in the comments directly above that line, through the end of the block the line
    opens (or the line itself, if it opens none). None if no line contains it.

    Parameters
    ----------
    sym : Symbol
        The symbol to narrow.
    focus : str
        Text on the line to start at.
    files : SourceFiles
        The source files.

    Returns
    -------
    Symbol or None
        A copy of `sym` over just that part, its first line as the signature and no doc;
        None if no line contains `focus`.
    """
    lines = files.lines(sym.file)
    first = next((n for n in range(sym.line, sym.end + 1) if focus in lines[n - 1]), None)
    if first is None:
        return None
    top = first
    while top - 1 > sym.start and lines[top - 2].strip().startswith(("//", "#")):
        top -= 1
    if sym.file.endswith(".py"):
        from codewalk.code.python import block_end

        return sym.model_copy(
            update={"start": top, "line": first, "end": block_end(lines, first, sym.end), "signature": lines[first - 1].strip(), "doc": ""}
        )
    depth, last = 0, first
    for n in range(first, sym.end + 1):
        code = lines[n - 1].split("//", 1)[0]
        opened = depth > 0 or "{" in code or "(" in code
        depth += code.count("{") + code.count("(") - code.count("}") - code.count(")")
        last = n
        if not opened or depth <= 0:
            break
    first_line = lines[first - 1].strip()
    return sym.model_copy(update={"start": top, "line": first, "end": last, "signature": first_line, "doc": ""})

# r[impl note.resolve]
# r[impl note.resolve-open]
def resolve(text: str, thread: Thread, mode: Literal["changelog", "remove"], date: str, about: list[str] | None = None) -> str:
    """`text` with a settled thread taken out: compacted into the changelog, or removed.

    Parameters
    ----------
    text : str
        The codewalk's Markdown.
    thread : Thread
        The thread, as parsed from `text`.
    mode : {"changelog", "remove"}
        Whether to keep a line of it in the changelog, a `## Changelog` section at the end
        (made if there isn't one), newest first.
    date : str
        Today, as ``YYYY-MM-DD``.
    about : list of str, optional
        The names it was about.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        The Markdown without the thread.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a question or request in it is still open.
    """
    if not thread.settled:
        raise ValueError("it's still open: answer or do what it asks first")
    lines = text.split("\n")
    start, end = thread.line - 1, thread.end
    # Take the thread and one blank line around it
    if start > 0 and not lines[start - 1].strip() and end < len(lines) and not lines[end].strip():
        start -= 1
    lines = lines[:start] + lines[end:]
    if mode == "changelog":
        entry = compact(thread, date, about)
        if CHANGELOG in lines:
            head = lines.index(CHANGELOG)
            stop = next((i for i in range(head + 1, len(lines)) if lines[i].startswith("#")), len(lines))
            first = next((i for i in range(head + 1, stop) if lines[i].startswith("- ")), None)
            if first is not None:
                lines = lines[:first] + [entry] + lines[first:]
            else:
                at = stop
                while at > head + 1 and not lines[at - 1].strip():
                    at -= 1
                lines = lines[:at] + ["", entry] + lines[at:]
        else:
            while lines and not lines[-1].strip():
                lines.pop()
            lines += ["", CHANGELOG, "", "What was asked here and how it was settled, newest first.", "", entry, ""]
    return "\n".join(lines)

# r[impl spec.drift]
def reconcile(ctx: Context, rel: str, rid: str | None = None) -> list[str]:
    """Record the prose citing a requirement, and the requirement, as they stand.

    That is, they say the same thing. All the cited requirements if `rid` is None.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ctx : Context
        The project.
    rel : str
        The spec file.
    rid : str or None
        The requirement; every cited one if None.

    Returns
    -------
    list of str
        The requirements reconciled; one cited but not defined is skipped.
    """
    walk = Walk(ctx, rel)
    known = ctx.spec
    blocks: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for _, _, block in _blocks(walk):
        for cid in cited_ids(block, known, rel):
            blocks.setdefault(cid, []).append(block)
    done = []
    for cid, texts in blocks.items():
        if (rid is None or cid == rid) and cid in known.requirements:
            prose = "\n\n".join(texts)
            ctx.review.mark(review_key(rel), f"{cid}#prose", _digest(prose), prose)
            ctx.review.mark(review_key(rel), f"{cid}#spec", _digest(known.requirements[cid].text), known.requirements[cid].text)
            done.append(cid)
    return done

# r[impl index.python-path]
def module_path(rel: str, root: Path | None = None) -> list[str]:
    """A file's dotted module name, as `::` segments.

    `codewalk/doc.py`, in a package `codewalk` (a folder with an `__init__.py`), is
    `codewalk::doc`, wherever the package sits. A file outside any package is its path from
    the root.

    Parameters
    ----------
    rel : str
        The file, from the root.
    root : Path or None
        The root; without it, the file is taken to be outside any package.

    Returns
    -------
    list of str
        The segments, without `__init__`.
    """
    path = Path(rel).with_suffix("")
    folder = (root / rel).parent if root else None
    if folder is None or not (folder / "__init__.py").exists():
        return [p for p in path.parts if p != "__init__"]
    parts = [] if path.name == "__init__" else [path.name]
    while folder != root and (folder / "__init__.py").exists():
        parts.insert(0, folder.name)
        folder = folder.parent
    return parts

def reply(text: str, thread: Thread, kind: Kind, author: str | None, body: str) -> str:

    lines = text.split("\n")

def init(root: Path, command: str | None = None, codewalks: str = "docs/codewalks", dry_run: bool = False) -> list[str]:
    """Set codewalk up in the project at `root`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : Path
        The project's root.
    command : str or None
        How to run codewalk there, for the docs and skills; worked out if None.
    codewalks : str
        Where codewalks go, from the root.
    dry_run : bool
        Report what it would do, and touch nothing.

    Returns
    -------
    list of str
        What it did (or would do), a line for each file.
    """
    package = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
    inside = package.is_relative_to(root)
    if command is None:
        command = f"uv run --project {os.path.relpath(package, root)} codewalk" if inside else "codewalk"
    # Linked when codewalk is in the project; outside it, there's nothing in the project to link to
    if inside:
        link = f"[codewalk]({os.path.relpath(package / 'README.md', root)})"
        syntax = f"[`SYNTAX.md`]({os.path.relpath(package / 'SYNTAX.md', root)})"
    else:
        link, syntax = "codewalk", "codewalk's own `SYNTAX.md`"
    install = ""
    if not inside:
        install = "\nIf `codewalk` isn't a command yet, install it from its repository with\n`uv tool install --editable .`.\n"
    values = {"codewalk": command, "codewalk_link": link, "codewalk_syntax": syntax, "install": install, "codewalks": codewalks}
    done: list[str] = []

    def write(rel: str, text: str, what: str) -> None:
        done.append(f"{'would ' + what if dry_run else PAST[what]}: {rel}")
        if not dry_run:
            path = root / rel
            path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            path.write_text(text)

    if not (root / "codewalk.toml").exists():
        langs = []
        if any(root.glob("src/**/*.rs")):
            langs.append('"src/**/*.rs"')
        if any(root.glob("src/**/*.py")) or any(root.glob("*/**/*.py")):
            langs.append('"**/*.py"')
        write("codewalk.toml", CONFIG.format(sources="[" + ", ".join(langs or ['"src/**/*.rs"']) + "]"), "write")

    section = f"{START}\n{_fill(_text('agents.md'), values).rstrip()}\n{END}\n"
    agents = root / "AGENTS.md"
    if agents.exists():
        current = agents.read_text()
        if START.split(" ")[0] in current and END in current:
            head = current[: current.index(START.split(" ")[0])]
            tail = current[current.index(END) + len(END) :].lstrip("\n")
            updated = head + section + ("\n" + tail if tail else "")
            if updated != current:
                write("AGENTS.md", updated, "update the codewalk section of")
        else:
            write("AGENTS.md", current.rstrip("\n") + "\n\n" + section, "add a codewalk section to")
    else:
        write("AGENTS.md", "# Contributing\n\n" + section, "write")

    for name, skill in (("codewalk-propose", "skill-propose.md"), ("codewalk-work", "skill-work.md")):
        rel = f".claude/skills/{name}/SKILL.md"
        text = _fill(_text(skill), values)
        if not (root / rel).exists() or (root / rel).read_text() != text:
            write(rel, text, "write the skill")
    return done

                thread = Thread(line=first[0] + 1 if first else 0, end=first[1] if first else 0, notes=notes)
                thread.about_line = last_block_line
                out.append((i, close, thread))
            i = close + 1
            continue
        if tok.level == 0 and tok.map and tok.nesting in (0, 1) and tok.type not in ("front_matter",):
            last_block_line = tok.map[0] + 1
        i += 1
    return out

    # r[impl serve.local]
    def start_prd(self, title: str, ask: str, source: str | None = None, thread: int | None = None) -> dict:
        """Start a PRD from the index, or from a thread in a codewalk, and say where to open it.

        From a thread, the PRD's request says which codewalk it came from, and a note added
        to the thread says where the PRD is.

        Parameters
        ----------
        title : str
            The PRD's title.
        ask : str
            What the person wants, in their own words.
        source : str or None
            The codewalk the thread is in, from the root, if it's started from one.
        thread : int or None
            The line the thread starts on.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            `started`, the PRD's path, and `href`, where to open it.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If there's a PRD by that name already, or the thread isn't there.
        """
        origin = None
        if source and thread:
            w = Walk(self.ctx, source)
            found = next((t for t in w.threads if t.line == thread), None)
            if found is None:
                raise ValueError(f"no thread on line {thread} of {source}")
            origin = (self.writable(source), found)
            ask = f"{ask.rstrip()}\n\nFrom [{w.title}]({os.path.relpath(source, prd.FOLDER)})."
        try:
            rel = prd.start(self.ctx, title, ask)
        except FileExistsError as e:
            raise ValueError(f"there's a PRD at {e} already") from e
        if origin:
            path, found = origin
            note = f"Taken up in a PRD: [{title}]({os.path.relpath(rel, os.path.dirname(source))})."
            path.write_text(notes.reply(path.read_text(), found, "note", self.ctx.config.who(self.ctx.root), note))
        return {"started": rel, "href": f"/walk/{rel}"}

    def _proposal(self, tok) -> Ref:
        """A `walk proposed` block, or `walk proposed change`: the name, then the draft."""
        lines = tok.content.rstrip("\n").split("\n")
        first = next((i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l.strip()), 0)
        words = tok.info.split()
        change = len(words) > 2 and words[2] == "change"

        ref = Ref(
            target=lines[first].strip() if lines else "",
            kind="proposal",
            line=line,
            proposed=True,
            change=change,
            draft="\n".join(lines[first + 1 :]).strip("\n"),
            lang=lang,
        )
        return self._resolve(ref)

# r[impl prd.check]

    def prd_problems(self) -> list[Problem]:
        """A PRD's spec checked against the spec, and anything written ahead of its stage."""
        if self.meta.kind != "prd":
            return []
        from codewalk.walk.prd import spec_changes

        changes = spec_changes(self)
        out = [Problem(severity="error", line=c.line, message=c.error or "") for c in changes if c.how == "error"]
        stage = self.meta.stage or "problem"
        at = STAGES.index(stage)
        ahead = [(c.line, "requirement") for c in changes if c.kind == "requirement" and at < STAGES.index("spec")]
        ahead += [(r.line, "proposal") for r in self.refs if r.kind == "proposal" and at < STAGES.index("code")]
        out += [Problem(severity="warning", line=line, message=f"a {what} at the {stage} stage") for line, what in ahead]
        return out

def spec_changes(w: Walk) -> list[SpecChange]:
    """What a PRD proposes for the spec, each against the spec as it stands.

    Parameters
    ----------
    w : Walk
        The PRD.

    Returns
    -------
    list of SpecChange
        In the order they're written in it.
    """
    ctx = w.ctx
    out = []
    for r in requirements.parse(w.rel, w.text, ctx.spec.prefixes, removals=True):
        now = ctx.spec.find(r.id)
        if now is None:
            how, error = ("error", f"removes `{r.id}`, which the spec doesn't have") if r.removed else ("new", None)
        elif r.version <= now.version:
            same = r.version == now.version and r.text == now.text and not r.removed
            message = f"changes `{r.id}` without a new version: the spec's is version {now.version}"
            how, error = ("quoted", None) if same else ("error", message)
        else:
            how, error = ("removed" if r.removed else "changed"), None
        was = now.text if now else None
        out.append(SpecChange(kind="requirement", id=r.id, line=r.line, version=r.version, how=how, text=r.text, was=was, error=error))
    for d in terms.parse(w.rel, w.text):
        now = ctx.glossary.get(f"{d.kind[0]}:{d.id}")
        how = "new" if now is None else "quoted" if now.text == d.text else "changed"
        out.append(SpecChange(kind=d.kind, id=d.id, line=d.line, how=how, text=d.text, was=now.text if now else None))
    return sorted(out, key=lambda c: c.line)

def start(ctx: Context, title: str, ask: str) -> str:
    """Start a PRD at `docs/prd/` and the title's slug, with what was asked as a request.

    ----------
    ctx : Context
        The project.
    title : str

    ask : str

        The PRD's path, from the root.

    Raises
    ------
    FileExistsError
        If there's a PRD there already.
    ValueError
        If the title has nothing a file can be named from.
    """
    name = slug(title)
    if not name:
        raise ValueError("a PRD needs a title with a letter or a number in it")

    target.write_text(notes.request(template(title), ctx.config.who(ctx.root), ask))
    return rel

# r[impl spec.prefix+2]
def parse(rel: str, text: str, prefixes: set[str], removals: bool = False) -> list[Requirement]:
    """The requirements in one file's text, in order, each with its version.

    Parameters
    ----------
    rel : str
        The file, from the root.
    text : str
        Its Markdown.
    prefixes : set of str
        The prefixes a requirement line can have, from `tracey::prefixes`.
    removals : bool
        Whether to read `r[id+N] removed` as a removal: in a PRD, and nowhere else.

    Returns
    -------
    list of Requirement
    """
    out = []
    lines = text.split("\n")
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        m = REQ.match(line)
        if not m or m.group(1) not in prefixes or (m.group(4) and not removals):
            continue
        body = []
        for nxt in lines[i + 1 :]:
            if not nxt.strip() or REQ.match(nxt):
                break
            body.append(nxt.strip())
        out.append(
            Requirement(
                id=tracey.key(m.group(1), m.group(2)),
                file=rel,
                line=i + 1,
                text="" if m.group(4) else " ".join(body),
                version=int(m.group(3) or 1),
                removed=bool(m.group(4)),
            )
        )
    return out

# r[impl term.define+2]
def parse(rel: str, text: str) -> list[Definition]:
    """The terms and facts defined in one file's text, in order.

    Parameters
    ----------
    rel : str
        The file, from the root.
    text : str
        Its Markdown.

    Returns
    -------
    list of Definition
    """
    out = []
    lines = text.split("\n")
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if not (m := DEF_LINE.match(line)):
            continue
        body = []
        for nxt in lines[i + 1 :]:
            if not nxt.strip() or DEF_LINE.match(nxt) or nxt.startswith("r["):
                break
            body.append(nxt.strip())
        kind = "term" if m.group(1) == "t" else "fact"
        # `cited-only` is a term's; a fact's status is one of the others
        if kind == "fact" and m.group(3) == "cited-only":
            continue
        status = (m.group(3) or "assumed") if kind == "fact" else None
        cited_only = m.group(3) == "cited-only"
        out.append(Definition(kind=kind, id=m.group(2), status=status, cited_only=cited_only, file=rel, line=i + 1, text=" ".join(body)))
    return out

# r[impl prd.start]
    # r[impl prd.from-thread]
    # r[impl serve.local]
    def start_prd(self, title: str, ask: str, source: str | None = None, thread: int | None = None) -> dict:
        """Start a PRD from the index, or from a thread in a codewalk, and say where to open it.

        From a thread, the PRD's request says which codewalk it came from, and a note added
        to the thread says where the PRD is.

        Parameters
        ----------
        title : str
            The PRD's title.
        ask : str
            What the person wants, in their own words.
        source : str or None
            The codewalk the thread is in, from the root, if it's started from one.
        thread : int or None
            The line the thread starts on.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            `started`, the PRD's path, and `href`, where to open it.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If there's a PRD by that name already, or the thread isn't there.
        """
        origin = None
        if source and thread:
            w = Walk(self.ctx, source)
            found = next((t for t in w.threads if t.line == thread), None)
            if found is None:
                raise ValueError(f"no thread on line {thread} of {source}")
            origin = (self.writable(source), found)
            ask = f"{ask.rstrip()}\n\nFrom [{w.title}]({os.path.relpath(source, prd.FOLDER)})."
        try:
            rel = prd.start(self.ctx, title, ask)
        except FileExistsError as e:
            raise ValueError(f"there's a PRD at {e} already") from e
        if origin:
            path, found = origin
            note = f"Taken up in a PRD: [{title}]({os.path.relpath(rel, os.path.dirname(source))})."
            path.write_text(notes.reply(path.read_text(), found, "note", self.ctx.config.who(self.ctx.root), note))
        return {"started": rel, "href": f"/walk/{rel}"}

# r[impl term.cite+2]
    def mentions(self) -> re.Pattern | None:
        """A pattern for every term as it's written in prose, but those cited only.

        Longest first, singular or plural, whole words only, ignoring case.

        Returns
        -------
        re.Pattern or None
            None if no terms are to be found in prose.
        """
        if self._pattern is None:
            words = sorted((d.words for d in self.terms.values() if not d.cited_only), key=len, reverse=True)
            alts = "|".join(re.escape(w).replace(r"\ ", r"[ \-]") for w in words)
            self._pattern = re.compile(rf"\b({alts})(?:s|es)?\b", re.IGNORECASE) if words else None
        return self._pattern

def test_a_prd_started_from_a_thread_and_the_thread_link_to_each_other(client, repo):
    (repo / "docs/walk.md").write_text("# Walk\n\n```walk\nMARGIN\n```\n\n> [!question] @m: Why hold back so much?\n")
    (thread,) = Walk(ctx(repo), "docs/walk.md").threads
    assert 'data-action="prd-from-thread"' in client.get("/walk/docs/walk.md").text
    r = client.post("/api/prd", json={"title": "Hold less", "ask": "Hold back less.", "source": "docs/walk.md", "thread": thread.line})

    request = Walk(ctx(repo), "docs/prd/hold-less.md").threads[0].notes[0]

    (thread,) = Walk(ctx(repo), "docs/walk.md").threads
    assert [(n.kind, n.text.strip()) for n in thread.all()][-1] == ("note", "Taken up in a PRD: [Hold less](prd/hold-less.md).")
    # A PRD's own threads don't offer it
    assert 'data-action="prd-from-thread"' not in client.get("/walk/docs/prd/hold-less.md").text
    bad = client.post("/api/prd", json={"title": "Other", "ask": "x", "source": "docs/walk.md", "thread": 1})
